title_content.content: Loar Holdings (LOAR) - covered by Noah Poponak

paragraph_content.content: LOAR is one of the highest quality Aerospace & Defense ‘earnings compounders,’ with very strong margins and free cash conversion, and still in the early stages of long-term growth and margin expansion. With revenues roughly twenty times smaller than competitor TDG, LOAR has ample balance sheet capacity, and is a preferred buyer in a very fragmented aerospace supply chain — providing the company with a long runway to acquire assets and supplement strong organic growth. All of this comes at a valuation discount to the average A&D supplier peers.

Long tail of acquisition opportunities. Early-stage M&A compounders have delivered the highest shareholder returns in aerospace over time. And as a preferred buyer in a very fragmented aerospace supply chain, Poponak sees a path for Loar to actively pursue a sustained tuck-in acquisition model. For example, LOAR recently made two acquisitions — LMB and Harper — that should supplement the company’s sector high organic growth rate, further boosting growth in 2026. Future M&A, which Poponak does not model, has the potential to add substantially to estimates.

- Strong organic growth meets very high margins. LOAR has the second highest organic growth rate among Poponak's covered aerospace suppliers, and the second best EBITDA margins, behind only TDG. In its latest results, LOAR delivered
yoy organic growth. And the top line is falling to the bottom line with adjusted EBITDA margins forecast to expand by 160bp in 2026 (to

- High commercial aerospace aftermarket mix. In its latest quarter, LOAR generated outsized revenue growth in its aftermarket business (+34% yoy). Aftermarket represents over half of LOAR revenues, comes at a higher margin, and continues to be fueled by increased global air traffic demand and the continued aging of the commercial fleet.

Poponak's estimates are above consensus across key financial metrics. He continues to believe the market underappreciates the duration of strength in the aerospace aftermarket, due to supply / demand imbalance in the large commercial aircraft fleet; and LOAR had particularly strong aftermarket growth in the quarter just reported. If that sustains through 2026 it drives further upside to estimates. The market also often underappreciates acquisition platform models operated in the aerospace supply chain, and LOAR just completed a flurry of deals, which will often then result in upside to earnings estimates as the consensus does not model the revenue and underestimates the margin power.

12-month price target of $100 based on a target 35.0X CY26E EV/EBITDA multiple which is informed by a peer group of other high-quality aerospace suppliers. Key risks: (1) Commercial & business jet end market demand, (2) DoW spending priorities, (3) M&A execution, and (4) Shareholder dilution.

Poponak expects LOAR to be able to beat and raise through 2026, with upside to consensus from a stronger aerospace aftermarket, margins, and deal integration. On its latest earnings call, management stated that the acquisition pipeline was busier than normal, and any incremental announcements could drive the stock. Positive reads from others in the aerospace supply chain are likely to occur, given strong demand for new aircraft, sustained strength in the aftermarket, and strong growth in defense verticals.

title_content.content: ServiceNow Inc. (NOW) – covered by Gabriela Borges

paragraph_content.content: Software incumbent with expanding platform breadth and a unique opportunity in AI.

May has been volatile for NOW: post an 18% sell off on 1Q EPS on 4/22, NOW has since recovered 28%, partly on improving sentiment post the analyst day and signs of green shoots in the app software space through off-cycle earnings. The key for sustained outperformance will be AI being additive to the WholeCo growth algorithm, and with NOW launching focused go to market motions for automating workflows like in IT Service Management, Gabriela Borges believes we are going into a catalyst-rich 2H. In its core business, Borges believes ServiceNow can sustain a ~20% organic CAGR through 2029 as it leans into still-robust expansion opportunities in new domains such as Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Human Capital Management (HCM). NOW has a unique position in the software space as it is a workflow engine (vs. a system of record). This IP translates to NOW being uniquely positioned as an orchestration engine managing AI deployments and, as it can deliver direct productivity improvements, taking share from the labor budgets in functions such the IT help desk. Lastly, NOW’s expanding real estate in the tech stack positions the company well for adjacencies in Security.

item_content.content: Business Transformation drives growth. NOW's transition from IT-centric workflows to an orchestration engine spanning multiple applications (ERP, CRM, HCM, etc.) is well underway. The company has increasingly applied its core workflow engine as a horizontal platform (the Now Platform) to drive productivity growth across existing ERP, CRM, and HCM systems. Look for continued expansion into adjacent workflows to drive a
organic CAGR through 2029.

The AI option. Borges believes NOW is one of the best positioned incumbent Software providers to establish itself as an orchestration layer across different knowledge workflows because it is already embedded across multiple enterprise workflows (ITSM broadly, HR, Finance, and increasingly CRM). Notably, NOW's Workflow Data Fabric and RaptorDB technology are foundational building blocks designed to support agentic deployment. She expects NOW to capture an increasing share of AI budgets, with medium-term opportunity as revenue contributions scale more meaningfully in 2027 as usage ramps.

- Expansion into Security. Borges sees a path where organic innovation creates a meaningful new product cycle for NOW over the next 5 years. Specifically, she thinks NOW is most likely to expand into select areas of Security, given the functionality sits adjacent to NOW’s existing position in the AI stack, leverages its core strengths, and is a large Total Addressable Market (TAM) to move the needle.

paragraph_content.content: Borges models market share by workflow to provide greater granularity into her organic growth forecasts and underwrite her 3 year ~20% organic revenue CAGR. Her application software framework for AI readiness assesses software vendors on their core tech stack; and ability to innovate and monetize AI. NOW screens well on this framework. Borges believes that ServiceNow is well positioned to drive GAAP margins higher in a market that rewards GAAP earnings, in part because the industry is shifting to an

operating model where opex growth is a function of compute, rather than a function of headcount growth. Finally, Borges spends an outsized amount of time evaluating the risk from software disintermediation in the enterprise tied to custom built tech stacks. Her investor conversations suggest that the pendulum has begun to swing back to packaged software offerings, and NOW in particular, as its AI platform has deepened.

12-month target price of $163 based on a 30x P/E multiple to ServiceNow's SNTM (Q5-Q8) non-GAAP earnings. Key downside risks include: 1) Slowing momentum in new market expansion reducing growth trajectory, 2) Lack of adoption of AI solutions and disintermediation of existing solutions by competitor AI technologies, and 3) Higher expense growth limiting margin expansion.

title_content.content: TPG Inc (TPG) - covered by Alex Blostein
Sustainable growth platform at a discounted valuation

paragraph_content.content: TPG shares are down almost 40% YTD alongside pressure on the broad alternative asset manager sector over concerns that the 15%+ annual growth it has seen over the last 3 years is unsustainable. But growth across private credit, wealth management, and even private equity remains much stronger than feared. TPG's Private Equity, Private Credit, and a re-emerging Real Estate funds are growing at a pace significantly above the industry as the firm's top-quartile performance enables market share consolidation. Look for base management fee growth of ~20% yoy in both 2026E and 2027E as AUM grows in its flagship private equity (PE) funds, investments in its Credit funds leads to management fee realization, and Real Estate fundraising begins contributing to management fees and fee related earnings (FRE). All of this should enable FRE margins to expand by 300bp this year (and ~100bps annually thereafter).

item_content.content: Core PE and Real Estate fund AUM going up. TPG is on track to raise ~$50bn of new Private Equity funds, growing assets vs prior vintages and gaining market share in an industry that rewards performance. TPG's flagship PE fund raise is driving ~20% management fee growth in '26E. Plus, TPG is planning to start a Real Estate fundraising cycle by year-end, further supporting management fee growth of ~20% in 2027.

Credit as a Growth Lever (really). Despite fears that the private credit market is facing challenges, Alex Blostein believes TPG's Credit business is fairly differentiated, and that institutional private credit investors remain dedicated to the asset class. In fact, TPG has indicated that demand for its Credit Solutions products (focused on customized capital solutions and bespoke financing) is the strongest it has ever seen - a dynamic amplified by the current backdrop of heightened volatility, credit market dispersion, and pockets of balance sheet stress that require tailored solutions. Importantly, this business carries structurally higher fee rates vs. more commoditized direct lending, supporting fee rate accretion over time. On the Direct Lending front, TPG's business is fairly differentiated with limited overlap with peers; to that end, its non-traded BDC saw only 1.3% redemption requests in 1Q (vs. industry average >10%).

Retail and Private Wealth AUM relatively underpenetrated. TPG's PE vehicle for its Wealth channel (think retail investors) - called TPOP — is now at ~$1.7bn of NAV, and the firm is planning on new distribution platform launches each quarter through year-end. TPG also generates fees from the TPG Private Markets Fund (TPM) and has already scaled to ~$415mn of NAV. Looking ahead, management has a pipeline of future products, including a multi-strategy credit fund, and a non-traded REIT, both of which should further expand TPG's retail footprint.

Margin Expansion. Look for TPG to generate FRE margins of 47.9% in 2026 — up 300bp from 2025 levels. Drivers include operating leverage, high-incremental-margin capital markets fees, and the favorable mix shift within Credit toward higher-fee Credit Solutions strategies. All of these factors should enable margin expansion beyond the mid-40s% range into 2027E and 2028E.

paragraph_content.content: Blostein's estimates are ~8% ahead of Visible Alpha consensus on average through '28E, as he looks for better fundraising follow-through (
50bn total in 2026), faster Credit deployment, and healthy upside to Real Estate fundraising cycle into 2027.

12-month target price of \$61 is based on a sum of the parts valuation of the various cash flows. Risks include: growing stock-based compensation, slower pace of fundraising, and less demand for ‘Impact’ and renewables fundraising

Progress on incremental fundraising for the TPG X and THP III funds; the first close of its new Real Estate funds; and evidence of improving backdrop to monetize PE investments, including strength in the IPO market.

Chicken strength should drive earnings growth. TSN's portfolio is diversified across protein categories, with exposure to beef (37% of FY24 sales), chicken (30%), prepared foods (18%), pork (11%), and international/other (4%). Jordan expects strong chicken demand to persist across both the retail and foodservice segments as it remains affordable relative to other proteins, driving future earnings growth. She also looks for additional support from recent distribution gains. Additionally, TSN's genetics business has returned to growth after years of investment, and the next leg of the story should ramp over the coming year as this is still a nascent opportunity for the company. Finally, while cattle costs remain an industry headwind amid tight supply, Jordan believes recent capacity closures should drive cost savings for TSN in 2H, especially amid early signs of regional herd rebuilding as rancher economics remain supportive, suggesting further profit recovery over the next few years

- Prepared foods resiliency. Look for prepared foods volume growth tied to heightened protein demand, distribution-driven market share gains, plus strong innovation. Additionally, TSN should be able to manage potential inflationary cost pressures supported by pricing, innovation/mix, strong volume demand, and partial vertical integration in select commodities, along with value engineering/ supplier programs for packaging costs. Look for further consumption growth ahead, especially in protein-related snacking, amid a sustained structural shift in dietary preferences towards protein-dense foods and an increased focus on nutrition.

Solid balance sheet. TSN's leverage has improved to 2.1x net debt/EBITDA (vs >4x two years ago), nearing its target of 2x or below. Continued FCF growth should support further improvement, which leaves the company plenty of optionality. In addition to a continued focus on maintaining financial strength and investing in the business, Jordan expects to see a step-up in returning cash to shareholders amid this stronger outlook. Of note, TSN restarted open market share repurchases, at a modest pace, in late FY25 (after a hiatus of ~2.5 years).

Jordan sits 2-3% higher than consensus EPS estimates for FY26/FY27 at $4.13/$4.67, respectively, primarily driven by tailwinds from strong demand, mix shifts toward its value-added products, and ongoing operational improvements, which is supported by her analysis of the company's brands and the commodity backdrop, along with the resilience of the protein category. Additionally, she believes the market is not fully appreciating the impact of its recent improvement in execution across its segments, with momentum building over the past few quarters, while she still sees plenty of runway for further improvement as it executes on a number of initiatives across its supply chain.

12-month target of $81 based on Jordan's risk-reward framework with a 50/50 blend of target P/E with downside/base/upside of 15x/16x/17x and target EV/EBITDA with downside/base/upside of 8x/8.5x/9x. Key downside risks include: a slowdown in economic activity, which could lead to a reduction in consumer spending, resulting in lower demand; shifts in consumption trends away from protein; margin pressure from increased promotional spending; higher raw material costs, including higher grain costs; lower packer margins; changes in regulation, which could result in higher costs; labor shortages or wage cost pressure; changes in tariffs; and loss of sales or higher costs related to an outbreak of food-borne illnesses or diseases among livestock.

title_content.content: UnitedHealth Group (UNH) - covered by Scott Fidel

paragraph_content.content: Shrink to grow insurer on the cusp of a pro-cyclical EPS reacceleration

UNH is on the cusp of seeing a bottom in the underwriting cycle for ~40% of its business — Medicare Advantage (MA) — a down cycle that has weighed significantly on the shares alongside similar downcycles in Medicaid and ACA exchanges. Look for the company to shrink its exposure to the MA end market at the same time as profitability in the market finds a bottom, leading to a sustained positive profit inflection for UNH. For 2026, Scott Fidel forecasts a 4% decline in MA Revenue but a ~50% increase in MA EBIT as the company prices exposures better and cuts costs partly through AI implementation — all helping to drive 15%+ EPS growth on average per year through 2028e.

Medicare Advantage about to get right. UNH is the largest MA provider and generates ~40% of total revenue from its MA health benefits business, though this revenue currently has a very small profit margin in the trough of the cycle. The MA market has faced three years of fundamental pressure from 2023-2025 as more patients (these are all people over 65) went to the doctor in the wake of the pandemic. And the 3-year MA underwriting down cycle was exacerbated by constrained 2024 and 2025 MA rate increases from CMS (the government rate setting agency), which companies broadly characterized as insufficient to cover higher trending medical expenses. With pricing resets now embedded and utilization trends coming in within management's cost assumptions, Fidel sees MA margins inflecting meaningfully from 2026 onward. Importantly, UNH is actively shrinking lower return MA exposure (more flexible PPO plans) while profitability improves, setting the stage for outsized incremental earnings leverage. Finally, Fidel believes that significant underlying earnings power was masked by elevated discretionary spending (including a huge ramp in incentive compensation) in 4Q25 and 1Q26. Looking ahead, as MA pricing exceeds medical costs, substantial profits should emerge from UNH's MA business in 2026 and beyond.

- Shrink to grow. In 2026, UNH plans to reduce MA membership (individual + group) by 1.3mn members, reduce its ACA Exchange footprint by ~one-third from a base of ~1.7mn members in 2025, and reduce OptumHealth's VBC membership by ~10%. All of these reductions are part of an effort to upscale the profit per member, drive higher sustained pricing, and improve margins. UNH is also leveraging AI technology in an effort to cut its operating cost ratio in half over time.

The good outweighs the bad. UNH is unlikely to put all of its troubles behind it over the next year. The company's Medicaid business is on pace to see margins decline by 130bp. And regulatory scrutiny around past CMS coding and healthcare access initiatives is ongoing. But the measures it is taking in right sizing its OptumHealth value based reimbursement segment began to yield results in 1Q26. Notably, as MA profitability improves, pressure on OptumHealth from elevated medical costs and operational noise eases, which should aid margin recovery in this segment. Fidel's work on the historical underwriting cycles within the US health insurance sector provides a unique lens into how typical the current environment is, even though it feels to some investors like a sea change. Bottom line, Fidel believes UNH represents a high conviction opportunity to own a best in class managed care franchise at the turning point of its earnings cycle. With MA margins bottoming, OptumHealth re accelerating, and cost normalization ahead, Fidel believes a durable, multi year EPS recovery is emerging that is not yet fully appreciated by the market.

12-month price target of $435 is based on a target P/E multiple of 19.1x Q5-Q8 estimated EPS. For context, UNH has traded at a 10-year average historical P/E of 18.8x within a range of ~13x-25x. Risks include elevated utilization, regulatory changes and scrutiny, pricing misalignment relative to utilization, and the potential for UNH to take a substantial charge to cover past claims.

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

paragraph_content.content: Buy (B), Neutral (N), Sell (S) Analysts recommend stocks as Buys or Sells for inclusion on various regional Investment Lists. Being assigned a Buy or Sell on an Investment List is determined by a stock's total return potential relative to its coverage universe. Any stock not assigned as a Buy or a Sell on an Investment List with an active rating (i.e., a stock that is not Rating Suspended, Not Rated, Early-Stage Biotech, Coverage Suspended or Not Covered), is deemed Neutral. Each region manages Regional Conviction Lists, which are selected from Buy rated stocks on the respective region's Investment Lists and represent investment recommendations focused on the size of the total return potential and/or the likelihood of the realization of the return across their respective areas of coverage. The addition or removal of stocks from such Conviction Lists are managed by the Investment Review Committee or other designated committee in each respective region and do not represent a change in the analysts' investment rating for such stocks.

Total return potential represents the upside or downside differential between the current share price and the price target, including all paid or anticipated dividends, expected during the time horizon associated with the price target. Price targets are required for all covered stocks. The total return potential, price target and associated time horizon are stated in each report adding or reiterating an Investment List membership.
Coverage Universe: A list of all stocks in each coverage universe is available by primary analyst, stock and coverage universe at https://www.gs.com/research/hedge.html.
